newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK, HUNGARIAN PMS TO SET MEETING DATE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK, HUNGARIAN PMS TO SET MEETING DATE.

text.p: The Slovak and Hungarian prime ministers on Friday will discuss a date for a detailed meeting on prickly issues dividing the two neighbours, an aide to Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said.
Meciar and his counterpart Gyula Horn had been due to meet in August in Komarno, southern Slovakia, to discuss a series of issues, but the meeting was abruptly cancelled by Meciar.
"They will probably try to set a date at their meeting today," Meciar's spokeswoman Magda Pospisilova told reporters. "Of course such a brief meeting cannot substitute detailed bilateral talks."
The two premiers are taking part in a summit meeting of CEFTA, the five-member Central European Free Trade Agreement, in the Slovak ski resort of Jasna on Friday and Saturday.

Relations between the two neighbours are cool due, in-part, to the controversy over Slovakia's treatment of its half-million ethnic Hungarian minority and Budapest's quitting a multi-million Danube dam project before its completion.

The Gabcikovo case, forcing Slovakia to divert a large part of the waters of the Danube which forms the border between the two countries, is to be brought before the International Court in the Hague next year. -- Jan Krcmar, Bratislava Newsroom 42-7 210 3687
